counterevidence_considered.description: The report contains a second rate with a subset-style denominator (telemetry completion 126/168 among inspected slots), which could superficially resemble the issue; however, it is labeled a secondary quality value, its denominator is the inspected set (which equals all 168 planned slots here), and the report states it does not define or enter the selected scientific endpoint.

source_refs.quoted_text:
Secondary quality value - telemetry completion among inspected slots: 126/168 = 0.75 (75%).
The quality denominator is inspected slots; it does not define or enter the selected scientific endpoint.

evidence.description: The selected result uses the complete planned domain in both numerator and denominator: 21/168 over all commissioned slots, matching the task's mandated target.

source_refs.quoted_text: [selected-result] Complete-calendar failure intensity over all commissioned slots: 21/168 = 0.125 (12.5%).

evidence.description: The workflow counts failure events over all commissioned (planned) rows, including screened-out slots whose failure column is populated (e.g., S128 and S136 are retained_after_screening=no with failure=yes), so the numerator as well as the denominator genuinely covers the complete domain rather than the retained subset (which contains only 15 of the 21 failures).
evidence.observed_value: events counted over planned_rows; removed-slot failures included

source_refs.quoted_text: events = sum(row["failure"] == "yes" for row in planned_rows)

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to demonstrate the issue two ways. First, I checked whether the 21-event numerator was derived only from retained slots and then spread over the 168-slot denominator; it was not — the data show failure outcomes recorded for screened-out slots (6 of the 21 failures come from removed slots) and the workflow sums failures over all planned rows, so the rate is a true complete-domain statistic. Second, I checked whether the secondary 126/168 quality value functions as the selected endpoint; the report explicitly designates the 21/168 line as the selected result and excludes the quality value from the endpoint. Both attempts fail, so the issue class is not present.
